problem: A component needs to render local UI state.
solution: Export a small model and update it with state.set().
tradeoffs: State is scoped to one component

problem: Multiple components need access to a page service or store.
solution: Inject the store through register(name, module, dependencies).

problem: Rendered children may be replaced during morphing.
solution: Use on(event, selector, callback) from main().
antiPatterns: Adding listeners to each repeated row

problem: The app should show useful content before JavaScript.
solution: Render semantic HTML first and add directives for dynamic fields.
tradeoffs: Requires backend and client state agreement

solution: Put render behavior in directives and update state explicitly.
antiPatterns: Manual textContent changes on Jails-owned nodes

problem: The feature should work acceptably without JavaScript.
solution: Use real links, forms, fallback text, and html-* delayed attributes.
tradeoffs: Client behavior may duplicate server routes
antiPatterns: Preventing all default navigation without fallback

problem: Expensive DOM behavior should not run until needed.
solution: Mount a small Jails component and dynamically import expensive code in main().
antiPatterns: Loading every widget dependency on page start

problem: User action should feel immediate while persistence is pending.
solution: Snapshot state, set optimistic state, rollback on failure.
antiPatterns: Changing DOM directly before state update

problem: A parent list renders state while each row has local behavior.
solution: Render child custom elements inside html-for and protect child-local state.
antiPatterns: Parent owning all transient row UI
